checks.title: Management group hierarchy, no subscription at the tenant root
checks.remediation: Create a management group hierarchy (platform, landing zones, sandbox) and move every subscription under it, so policy and role assignments inherit.
checks.narrative: A subscription at the tenant root inherits nothing: no benchmark, no policy, no standing-access rules. Management groups are where those are set once.

checks.title: Microsoft cloud security benchmark assigned on every subscription
checks.remediation: Enable Defender for Cloud on the listed subscriptions, or assign the benchmark initiative at the management group so new subscriptions inherit it.
checks.narrative: The benchmark is the policy set behind Azure Secure Score and every Defender for Cloud recommendation. A subscription without it is unevaluated, not clean.

checks.title: Defender for Cloud plans on where the resource types exist
checks.remediation: Turn on the Defender plan for each listed subscription and resource type: Servers, Storage, Key Vault, Databases, Containers, App Service, APIs, and Resource Manager everywhere.
checks.narrative: The plans are the paid detections: runtime threat detection on VMs, malware scanning on storage, anomalous Key Vault access. Off on a subscription that holds the resource is the finding; off elsewhere is fine and noted.

checks.title: Defender CSPM enabled
checks.remediation: Enable Defender CSPM on the subscriptions where attack paths, permissions creep and unused-permission findings are wanted.
checks.narrative: Defender CSPM adds attack path analysis and the identity findings Entra Permissions Management used to carry. Without it those rows are not evaluated.

checks.title: Security contact with alert notifications on every subscription
checks.remediation: Set a security contact email on each listed subscription with alert notifications for high severity and above, and the Owner role notified.
checks.narrative: Defender for Cloud alerts that nobody is emailed about sit in the portal. The contact is who finds out.

checks.title: Activity log exported from every subscription
checks.remediation: Add a diagnostic setting on each listed subscription that sends the activity log categories to the Log Analytics workspace or Sentinel, with a year or more of retention there.
checks.narrative: The activity log holds every control-plane change and is kept 90 days on its own. The export is what makes an investigation older than that possible.

checks.title: Delete locks on Key Vaults and Recovery Services vaults
checks.remediation: Apply a CanNotDelete lock to each listed vault, or to its resource group.
checks.narrative: A Key Vault or backup vault deleted by mistake, or by an attacker with Contributor, is the outage and the ransomware scenario in one. The lock is cheap.

checks.title: Policy coverage beyond the benchmark on every subscription
checks.remediation: Assign the organisation's own policies (deny public IPs, deny public storage, require encryption, allowed locations) at the management group.
checks.narrative: The benchmark audits. The organisation's own deny policies are what stop a misconfiguration from being created at all.

checks.title: Owner and environment tags on the fleet
checks.remediation: Enforce the owner and environment tags with a policy that inherits them from the resource group, then tag the resource groups.
checks.narrative: A resource with no owner tag is a resource nobody will answer for when the finding lands. Tags are the join key between the posture report and the people.

checks.title: No orphaned resources
checks.remediation: Delete the unattached disks, unused public IPs, NICs without a VM and empty resource groups, or document why each stays.
checks.narrative: Orphans cost money and carry data: an unattached disk still holds the VM's contents. The counts are the clean-up list.

checks.title: Owners per subscription within the limit, none synced from AD
checks.remediation: Reduce standing Owners to three or fewer named cloud-only accounts per subscription; everyone else gets Contributor or an eligible PIM assignment.
checks.narrative: Owner on a subscription is full control including the right to grant it. Owners inherited from the root or a management group count too; synced accounts tie the subscription's fate to on-premises AD.

checks.title: No standing Owner or User Access Administrator at root or management group
checks.remediation: Remove the standing assignments at the root and management group scopes and make them eligible through PIM for Azure resources.
checks.narrative: A permanent Owner at the root scope owns every subscription that exists and every one created later. Eligible is the only acceptable state for that role.

checks.title: No guest users with Azure role assignments
checks.remediation: Remove the guest assignments, or record each as an object-level exception with the partner and the reason.
checks.narrative: A guest with an Azure role is a partner's account, governed by the partner's MFA and lifecycle, with rights in your subscription.

checks.title: Service principals with Owner or Contributor justified
checks.remediation: Record each listed service principal as an exception with its purpose, prefer a managed identity over an app secret, and scope it to a resource group rather than the subscription.
checks.narrative: A service principal with Contributor is a credential that can rebuild the subscription. Pipelines need it; the question is which ones and at what scope.

checks.title: No orphaned role assignments
checks.remediation: Delete the assignments whose principal no longer exists.
checks.narrative: An assignment to a deleted principal is noise now and a grant to whoever recreates the object id later. They accumulate with every leaver.

checks.title: No custom roles with wildcard actions
checks.remediation: Rewrite the listed custom roles with explicit actions; a role that grants * is Owner with a different name.
checks.narrative: Wildcard actions in a custom role defeat the point of the custom role and hide an Owner-equivalent grant from every review that looks for Owner.

checks.title: No classic administrators
checks.remediation: Remove the listed Co-Administrators and Service Administrators; the role type was retired in 2024 and anything left is unmanaged access.
checks.narrative: Classic administrators sit outside RBAC and PIM. Microsoft retired the type; a tenant that still has them has access nobody reviews.

checks.title: Role assignments to individual users at resource scope within the limit
checks.remediation: Replace per-user assignments on individual resources with group assignments at resource group scope; the count is the trend to drive down.
checks.narrative: Hundreds of per-user grants on individual resources are unreviewable. Groups at resource group scope are the maintainable shape.

checks.title: Key Vaults on the RBAC model with purge protection, soft delete and no public access
checks.remediation: Switch each listed vault to RBAC authorisation, enable purge protection and soft delete, and disable public network access or set the firewall default to deny.
checks.narrative: Key Vault holds the secrets everything else depends on. Access policies are the legacy model nobody reviews; purge protection is what stops an attacker deleting the keys for good.

checks.title: Storage accounts without shared keys, anonymous blobs or HTTP
checks.remediation: Disable shared key access and anonymous blob access on each listed account, require HTTPS and TLS 1.2; move clients to Entra authentication or SAS tokens scoped and dated.
checks.narrative: A storage account key is a password to every byte in the account, and anonymous blob access is the classic public-bucket leak. Both are off by one switch each.

checks.title: Azure SQL servers on Entra-only authentication
checks.remediation: Enable Entra-only authentication on each listed SQL server once the applications use managed identities or Entra logins.
checks.narrative: SQL authentication is a password in a connection string. Entra-only removes it as a path, the same move as disabling shared keys on storage.

checks.title: Conditional Access covers the Azure management plane
checks.remediation: Create a Conditional Access policy that targets Windows Azure Service Management API (Microsoft Azure Management) for all users and requires MFA or a phishing-resistant strength and a compliant device.
checks.narrative: The portal, CLI and ARM API are all the management plane. A policy on all cloud apps covers it; a tenant with app-specific policies often leaves it out.
